entries.what_happened: Three manuscripts make temperedness claims, all over function fields F = F_q(X). (1) Ramanujan-Arthur Decompositions of Cuspidal Functions at Full Finite Level, Corollary 1.2: for split connected adjoint absolutely simple G, a cuspidal automorphic representation with one generic unramified local component is tempered at every unramified place. The proof forces the orbit label at the good places to be zero, using the local criterion of Ciubotaru-Harris (their Corollary 6.32(1)), and the paper says the common orbit removes the tempered-place hypothesis of their Theorem 5.4. (2) Temperedness at ramified places for globally generic exceptional groups, Theorem 1: for split connected adjoint absolutely simple G of type G2, F4, E6, E7 or E8, every local component of a globally generic cuspidal automorphic representation of G(A_F) is tempered at every place, ramified places included, with no restriction on characteristic or ramification depth. It takes the unramified places from (1) and reaches the ramified places through a pure-completion local criterion (Theorem thm:local-criterion). (3) Global Arthur Enhancements of Cuspidal Excursion Parameters gives no temperedness conclusion. It produces an SL_2 factor and a centralizer part of weight zero, so Frobenius eigenvalues have absolute value one only on the centralizer part, not in general. Rationality of the Canonical Unramified Arthur Filtration, The Restricted Geometric Langlands Equivalence in Positive Characteristic, and the three tame Hecke eigensheaf manuscripts do not bear on temperedness.
entries.delivers: Function fields only, and only for generic cuspidal representations. The two temperedness results have different scopes. Temperedness paper: globally generic cuspidal representations, exceptional split adjoint absolutely simple G, all places. Ramanujan-Arthur Corollary 1.2: one generic unramified local component suffices, any split adjoint absolutely simple G (this includes PGL_n), unramified places only. The abstract of the Temperedness paper says it proves the generalized Ramanujan conjecture for the globally generic exceptional case; that is the scope of the claim, not the conjecture in full. For GL_n over function fields the family adds nothing new: the Temperedness introduction records that Laurent Lafforgue proved Ramanujan for GL_n. Not covered: the holomorphic Petersson bound (part a) and the Maass-form statement (part b), which concern number fields such as Q; no manuscript in the family addresses them. Also not covered: non-generic cuspidal representations.
entries.remains: If the claims are correct: temperedness for non-generic cuspidal representations, which the Ramanujan-Arthur decomposition places into orbit summands but does not bound; unramified places for cuspidal representations with no generic unramified local component; ramified places for split adjoint absolutely simple groups outside the five exceptional types, since the headline theorem does not state them (see doubts); number fields and parts (a) and (b); non-adjoint and non-split groups.
entries.direction: proves a case: generic cuspidal representations are tempered (all places for exceptional adjoint groups; unramified places for split adjoint absolutely simple groups from one generic unramified component)
entries.conditional_on: The Temperedness paper's unramified step is Ramanujan-Arthur Corollary 1.2, which relies on the Ciubotaru-Harris local criterion (their Corollary 6.32(1)), an external result not proved in the family. The Temperedness paper also takes these as cited inputs: Lafforgue and Genestier-Lafforgue parameters and local-global compatibility (Theorem thm:parameters); the Gan-Harris-Sawin tempered completion (Theorem thm:tempered-completion); the Gan-Lomeli globalization theorem and Lomeli's crude functional equation for the local-coefficient comparison; and Deligne's theorem on weights of local monodromy (Weil II, 1.8.4). The Ramanujan-Arthur Corollary 1.2 also uses V. Lafforgue's global parameter theorem.
entries.doubts: (i) The headline theorem is limited to G2, F4, E6, E7 and E8, but the local criterion (Theorem thm:local-criterion) and the global argument in sections/global.tex are stated for any split adjoint absolutely simple group, and the introduction says generic Ramanujan for split classical groups was already proved by Lomeli. The text gives no reason for the exceptional restriction, and I did not find a step in the parts I read that uses exceptionality. (ii) The removal of Ciubotaru-Harris's tempered-place hypothesis in Corollary 1.2 is asserted in the text and rests on applying their Corollary 6.32(1); I did not check that application. (iii) Corollary 1.2 rests on the local decomposition theorem (Theorem ext:discrete, in the sections on the local geometry), which I did not read. A search of these manuscripts for sketch-type hedges found none in the parts that bear on temperedness.

entries.what_happened: Four manuscripts engage Arthur's conjectures. None proves a packet-level statement. (1) Global Arthur Enhancements of Cuspidal Excursion Parameters: assuming the finite-level Ramanujan-Arthur decomposition (its Theorem 1.1, cited as Parent), for each occurring excursion character nu of a split connected semisimple group over a global function field, at any full finite level, it constructs an algebraic SL_2 homomorphism phi_nu into the dual group, whose differential sends the raising element into the nilpotent orbit O_nu given by the decomposition, and a continuous homomorphism tau_nu from the Weil group W_U into the algebraic centralizer of phi_nu(SL_2), with reductive Zariski closure and eigenvalues of absolute value one at every complex embedding, such that after one fixed conjugation sigma_nu(w) = tau_nu(w) phi_nu(diag(a^deg(w), a^-deg(w))) for all w in W_U, inertia included. (2) Ramanujan-Arthur Decompositions of Cuspidal Functions at Full Finite Level, unconditionally: for split semisimple G over a global function field, the cuspidal function space at any full finite level, with arbitrary divisor multiplicities, splits as a direct sum over nilpotent orbits of the dual group, both rationally and over Q-bar_ell. At level zero this proves Conjectures 3.4.5 and 3.4.6 of Gaitsgory-Lafforgue-Raskin. (3) Rationality of the Canonical Unramified Arthur Filtration: for split connected semisimple G, under four characteristic conditions, the canonical filtration on finitely supported unramified automorphic functions is defined over Q for every closed invariant nilpotent support. The paper presents this as Conjecture 2.7.3 of Gaitsgory-Lafforgue-Raskin. Its cuspidal corollary identifies the level-zero cuspidal part with the rational orbit summands of (2), which the paper calls the common-scope form of Conjectures 3.4.9 and 3.4.11. (4) The Temperedness paper and Ramanujan-Arthur Corollary 1.2 give only generic-case temperedness, which the problem's lead names as a consequence of Arthur's conjectures; see the ramanujan-petersson-conjecture entry. The Restricted Geometric Langlands full-support manuscript and the three tame Hecke eigensheaf manuscripts do not bear on Arthur's conjectures. They concern geometric Langlands support and eigensheaves with tame unipotent monodromy, and make no claim about Arthur parameters, packets or SL_2 factors.
entries.delivers: Each of (1)-(3) is a Galois-side or spectral-support structure over function fields for split groups: a commuting SL_2 and weight-zero centralizer pair recovering each occurring excursion parameter, an orbit decomposition of cusp spaces, and rationality of a canonical Arthur filtration. None states or proves the global Arthur packet decomposition of the discrete spectrum, local Arthur packets, unitarity of packet members, or the multiplicity formula. The Global Arthur paper says explicitly that it asserts no ellipticity, no Arthur-packet classification and no multiplicity formula. No manuscript claims to settle Arthur's conjectures. The family's result is function-field and split-group only, so the number-field content of the problem's lead is outside it. The text frames the commuting pair as the parameter-level part of V. Lafforgue's Arthur conjecture, whose elliptic form it does not prove. Whether the Galois-side pair counts as an Arthur-type parameter for the statement is for the judging pass to decide.
entries.remains: If the claims are correct, the parts of the problem's list not covered are still open as far as this family goes: global and local Arthur packets and their character identities, Arthur's multiplicity formula, unitarity of packet members, the 1989 unipotent conjectures, and ellipticity of the global parameter (V. Lafforgue's version, not claimed here). For the generalized Ramanujan part, the family gives generic-case temperedness only. Also open: the enhancement is existential, with no uniqueness or multiplicity statement, and no link to packets is made.
entries.direction: constructs Galois-side Arthur-type data over function fields (an SL_2 and weight-zero centralizer pair per occurring excursion parameter), proves an orbit decomposition of cusp spaces, and proves rationality of a canonical Arthur filtration; no packets
entries.object: phi_nu: SL_2 into the dual group and tau_nu: W_U into the centralizer of phi_nu(SL_2), attached to each occurring excursion character. Constructed by an existence argument (the proof of Theorem thm:main proceeds by contradiction); not explicit.
entries.conditional_on: Global Arthur Enhancements assumes the finite-level Ramanujan-Arthur decomposition (Theorem 1.1 of the Ramanujan-Arthur paper, restated there as thm:parent) and uses further results of that paper, cited as Parent: Sections 2-3, Lemma 6.4, Theorems 2.2-2.3, Propositions 2.5-2.7 and Lemma 3.6. It also cites external inputs: Xue's finiteness and smoothness theorems for stacks of shtukas, the nearby-cycle comparisons of Salmon and Eteve-Xue, Laurent Lafforgue's purity theorem, and Bezrukavnikov and Ben-Zvi-Chen-Helm-Nadler for the local coherent models. Rationality of the Canonical Unramified Arthur Filtration assumes the four characteristic conditions of restricted geometric Langlands theory and uses the restricted equivalence and trace inputs of AGKRRV, Gaitsgory-Raskin and Raskin as cited. Its cuspidal corollary depends on the Ramanujan-Arthur paper (Theorem 1.1, Lemmas 6.1-6.2, Propositions 6.5-6.6, Remark 6.3).
entries.doubts: (i) thm:parent in the Global Arthur paper is stated for occurring excursion characters, but the decomposition it cites (Theorem 1.1 of the Ramanujan-Arthur paper) is stated for joint eigencharacters of spherical Hecke operators at good places. The passage between the two is asserted with a citation; I did not verify it. (ii) The Global Arthur proof is a contradiction argument of about 5,400 lines. I did not read the lemmas it depends on, such as lem:tensor-nilpotence, prop:ind-qc-comparison and prop:open-orbit-enhancement. (iii) The Rationality paper flags a scope caveat itself: its pure Weil lift input (Theorem inp:pure-lift) is cited to a proposition stated for irreducible Weil parameters, and the paper uses a semisimple consequence recorded in a GLR appendix. A search of these manuscripts for sketch-type hedges found none in the parts that bear on Arthur's conjectures.
